planning-self-regulation/implementation-.reason: No bias-corrected estimate near zero and no failed large replication found (searched). The 642-test meta-analysis reports .27 <= d <= .66 (no correction in its abstract); the pre-registered alcohol meta-analysis is smaller but positive (d+ = -0.14 weekly drinking; trim-and-fill found zero missing studies). Effect 'moderate' sits at the low edge. Carrera et al. 2018 (n = 877) is a tightly estimated null for scheduling a repeated behaviour (gym visits): a boundary condition, not a tie-break 1 replication. The 2021 gym megastudy cannot isolate planning, since 53 of 54 arms included a planning prompt.

Cooke, McEwan & Norman (2023), Drug and Alcohol Review
Carrera, Royer, Stehr, Sydnor & Taubinsky (2018), Journal of Health Economics

planning-self-regulation/progress-monito.reason: Tie-break 4. Harkin et al.'s full text (author manuscript, eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/87431) reports goal-attainment heterogeneity 'Q(137) = 837.77' (I-squared about 84%). The two reported moderators that match a private paper page pull apart: 'monitoring in private (d+ = 0.19)' against 'Physically recording the information ... (d+ = 0.43)'. No private-and-recorded subgroup is reported, so the heterogeneity is not resolved for our conditions. Trim-and-fill gives 'd+ = 0.19 (95% CI = 0.10 to 0.28)', which is not near zero, so tie-break 2 does not fire. Effect should become small. Displayed grades of check-in, Ritual and scoresheet are unchanged, because prior-state-recall is already C.

sources.cite: Harkin et al. (2016), Psychological Bulletin (full-text author manuscript)

planning-self-regulation/progress-monito.helps_overclaim: check-in, Ritual, scoresheet: if the effect becomes small (the matching private-monitoring subgroup is d+ = 0.19), tie-break 7 requires the helps text to say the gain is small. Check-in's 'helps goal attainment more when physically recorded' does not.
